description: Fix the sequential-mode wrapper-commit so it commits only the changes an iteration produced, instead of sweeping pre-existing dirty/untracked working-tree files in with `git add -A`. Capture a pre-iteration `git status` baseline and stage only the set difference.

criteria: Rust: No warnings in `cargo check` output
Rust: No warnings in `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` output
Rust: Scoped tests pass with `cargo test -p task-mgr <module>` (full suite at REVIEW-001)
No breaking changes to existing public APIs unless explicitly required (wrapper_commit is pub(crate) — its signature change is in-scope)
Status mutations (if any) go through TaskLifecycle, never raw UPDATE SQL — N/A for this change (no status writes)
globalAcceptanceCriteria.description: These criteria apply to ALL implementation tasks

priorityPhilosophy.description: Hierarchy of what matters most when implementing tasks
hierarchy: 1. PLAN — Anticipate edge cases before coding
2. PHASE 2 FOUNDATION — ~1 day now to save ~2+ weeks later (1:10+ ratio); we are pre-launch, foundations compound
3. FUNCTIONING CODE — Pragmatic, reliable, wired in per plan
4. CORRECTNESS — Compiles, type-checks, scoped tests pass deterministically
5. CODE QUALITY — Clean code, qualityDimensions satisfied, no warnings
principles: Quality dimensions explicit — qualityDimensions on every task tells you what 'good' looks like
Safety over convenience — when the baseline is unknown, SKIP the commit rather than risk sweeping; never fall back to `git add -A`
Edge cases = test cases — every known edge case must have a corresponding test
Scoped per-iteration tests, full suite at REVIEW-001 — REVIEW must leave the trunk green including pre-existing failures
Ship working code with tests to prove it; handle Option/Result explicitly; avoid unwrap() in production

prohibitedOutcomes: Any `git add -A` (or `git add .`) WITHOUT a `-- <pathspec>` scope in the wrapper-commit path — that is the exact bug being fixed
Falling back to staging everything when the baseline is None — must skip+warn instead
Tests that only assert 'no crash' or check the return type without verifying which paths were committed vs left dirty
A `-z` parser that mis-handles rename entries (off-by-one consuming the FROM field) or treats the Y status slot as a rename indicator
Committing gitignored or pre-existing-dirty files (the regression this fix exists to prevent)
Error messages that don't identify what went wrong

acceptanceCriteria: Positive: capture_status_paths runs `git status --porcelain -z --untracked-files=all` and returns a HashSet<String> of paths; renames contribute both TO and FROM paths.
Positive: wrapper_commit with a baseline stages exactly `current - baseline` via `git add -A -- <paths>`, then commits.
Negative: wrapper_commit must NOT invoke `git add -A` without a `-- <pathspec>` anywhere in the function.
Negative: a None baseline returns None and emits a `ui::emit` warning — must NOT stage anything.
Unit test (parser): a renamed tracked file yields BOTH old and new paths in the returned set.
Unit test (parser): an entry whose Y slot is R/C but X is not (e.g. ` R`) is NOT treated as a rename (no phantom FROM consumption); trailing empty split field is dropped.
Unit test (happy parity): clean tree at baseline, agent creates foo.rs → only foo.rs committed (matches what `git add -A` would have produced on a clean tree).
Unit test (exclusion): baseline has untracked stray.md; agent creates foo.rs → only foo.rs committed; stray.md remains on disk, untracked, after the commit.
Unit test (untracked-dir granularity): baseline has untracked data/old.md; agent creates data/new.md → data/new.md committed, data/old.md not.
Unit test (tracked exclusion): baseline has modified tracked a.txt; agent modifies b.txt → only b.txt committed; a.txt change still uncommitted.
Unit test (deletion): agent deletes a tracked file → the commit contains its removal.
Unit test (nothing-new): agent touches only a baseline-dirty path → wrapper_commit returns None, no commit created.
Unit test (None baseline): wrapper_commit(.., None) returns None, creates no commit, sweeps nothing.
CONTRACT: the call site in src/loop_engine/reactions/post_completion.rs (the `for id in completed_ids` loop) compiles against the new 4-arg signature (updated in FEAT-002).
userStories.description:
Rewrite the sequential wrapper-commit staging in src/loop_engine/git_reconcile.rs so it commits only paths the iteration produced.

DO:
- Add `pub(crate) fn capture_status_paths(working_root: &Path) -> Option<HashSet<String>>` that runs `git status --porcelain -z --untracked-files=all` and parses the NUL-separated entries into a set of paths. Each entry is `XY<sp><path>`; for a rename/copy entry the form is `XY<sp>TO\0FROM\0` — insert BOTH the new (TO) and old (FROM) paths. Return None ONLY if the git invocation itself fails.
- Change `wrapper_commit` signature to `wrapper_commit(working_root: &Path, task_id: &str, message_suffix: &str, baseline: Option<&HashSet<String>>) -> Option<String>`.
- New body: `let baseline = baseline?;` (None → emit ONE `ui::emit` line saying the agent didn't commit and the wrapper can't safely stage so the work was left dirty, then return None — NEVER `git add -A`). Then `let current = capture_status_paths(working_root)?;` compute `current.difference(baseline)`; if empty return None; else stage with `git add -A -- <paths...>`; commit + rev-parse logic unchanged.
- Add a rustdoc note on wrapper_commit documenting the deliberate footgun: a path dirty at baseline that the agent ALSO edits is excluded (its change stays uncommitted in the tree — visible, not lost; correct for a loop worktree expected clean at start).

DO NOT:
- Use `git add -A` without a `-- <pathspec>` scope.
- Key the rename/copy detection on the Y slot — renames are index-side (X slot only: `entry.as_bytes()[0] == b'R' || == b'C'`).
- Forget to drop the trailing empty field produced by splitting `-z` output on NUL.
- Use porcelain v2 — v1 `-z` is sufficient and simpler.

Edge cases:
- Untracked file inside a PRE-EXISTING untracked directory: `--untracked-files=all` gives file granularity so the agent's new file is committed while the sibling stray is not.
- Agent deletes a tracked file: `git add -A -- <path>` stages the deletion.
- gitignored files (e.g. tasks/progress-*.txt) never appear in `git status --porcelain`, so they are naturally excluded — no special-casing.

Known-bad to guard against:
- A naive `git add -- <paths>` (no `-A`) stages deletions only on git >=2.0 — use `-A -- <paths>`.
- Splitting `-z` on NUL and treating every token as a separate path double-counts the FROM field of a rename as a phantom path.
edgeCases: None baseline (git status failed upstream): return None + ui::emit warning, leave tree dirty
Empty diff (agent touched only baseline-dirty paths): return None, no commit
New file inside a pre-existing untracked directory: committed at file granularity
Agent-deleted tracked file: deletion staged via `git add -A -- <path>`
Rename/copy entry: both old and new paths captured
gitignored progress file dirty during iteration: absent from porcelain, naturally excluded

failureModes.cause: git status invocation fails (not a repo / git missing)
failureModes.expectedBehavior: capture_status_paths returns None → wrapper_commit returns None with a ui::emit warning; no partial staging

failureModes.cause: Pathological iteration with thousands of changed paths exceeding ARG_MAX on `git add -A -- <paths>`
failureModes.expectedBehavior: Acceptable for v1 (far worse cases pre-date this); note in rustdoc as a known limit. Do NOT silently truncate.

userStories.notes: Reuse: rename-handling intent from worktree.rs:2401-2413 (`dirty_tracked_paths`, column-based) adapted for `-z`; selective-add pattern from worktree.rs:2444-2446 (`git add -- <vec>`). Test harness: `test_utils::init_test_repo()` returns (TempDir, PathBuf) with an initial commit; `setup_git_repo_with_file()` writes file.txt. Tests shell out to git via std::process::Command (fine in cargo test). Existing tests start at git_reconcile.rs:456 (`#[cfg(test)] mod tests`) — add new tests there; there is currently NO direct wrapper_commit test. Learning 5270: feature branches accumulate unrelated dirty files (task JSON, progress, command files) — staging discipline must scope to the iteration's own changes. Learning 1808/2966/3302: tasks/progress-*.txt are gitignored, never appear in porcelain output. Learning 2445: untracked entries need explicit flags (parallels `--untracked-files=all`). Learning 4747: when these tests run under the loop, git mutations need sandbox disabled.
qualityDimensions: Set-difference semantics: stage exactly current-minus-baseline by path; never widen to `-A` unscoped
`-z` parser correctness: rename keyed on X slot only, both TO+FROM inserted, trailing empty field dropped, no phantom paths
Fail-safe on None baseline: skip + visible `ui::emit` warning, never sweep
Tests verify WHICH paths landed in the commit and which stayed dirty — not just a non-None return
Idiomatic: reuse existing git-command + porcelain patterns from worktree.rs; no new abstractions

userStories.description:
Wire the pre-iteration baseline from run_loop into wrapper_commit, and update the call site to the new 4-arg signature.

DO:
- Add field `git_status_baseline: Option<&'a HashSet<String>>` to `PostCompletionParams<'a>` (src/loop_engine/reactions/post_completion.rs ~71-94).
- Add it to the EXHAUSTIVE destructure in `react_to_completions_inner` (~218-229) and pass it to the `wrapper_commit(working_root, id, "loop wrapper commit", git_status_baseline)` call (~237).
- In orchestrator.rs run_loop: immediately BEFORE the `run_iteration(&mut ctx, &mut iteration_params)` call (~329) capture `let git_baseline = git_reconcile::capture_status_paths(&working_root);` and pass `git_status_baseline: git_baseline.as_ref()` in the sequential PostCompletionParams construction (~422).
- Pass `git_status_baseline: None` at the wave construction (wave_scheduler.rs ~1381, wrapper_commit=false), the human-review compat shim (orchestrator.rs ~912), and the parity-test helper (tests/reaction_parity.rs ~2282).
- Docs (same commit): update the post_completion.rs ~189-193 rustdoc that describes the old `git status --porcelain` no-op, and the wrapper-commit row context in src/loop_engine/CLAUDE.md:558, to the baseline-diff contract (the 'at most one commit per iteration' invariant still holds; the reason changes from 'tree clean' to 'no NEW paths remain').

DO NOT:
- Capture the baseline INSIDE run_iteration or thread it through IterationResult (14 construction sites) — capture in run_loop's scope where PostCompletionParams is built.
- Capture the baseline AFTER run_iteration returns — it must be snapshotted before the agent runs.
- Set `git_status_baseline` to anything but None on the wave / shim / parity-test paths (wrapper_commit is false there; a real value would be unused but misleading).

Edge cases:
- run_iteration only mutates DB/signals before the agent spawn (the sequential claim is DB-only — no `with_prd_sync`), so the run_loop-captured baseline accurately reflects pre-task tree state. Verify this still holds (grep the claim path) and keep it true.

First iteration with a clean tree: baseline is an empty set, diff == all agent changes (parity with old behavior)
